headline.purpose: Section headings; the close uses a larger 900/140% setting.

title.purpose: Answer headings on the answer sheet.

speech.purpose: The duck's question in the speech bubble.

body.purpose: Running text, ledes at 62ch, answers at 52ch.

label.purpose: Uppercase wide labels: board and matrix column headers, the docs mark pill.

code.purpose: Code blocks, install command, API/package/test names, board cells, readouts.

reading.purpose: Docs prose on the sheet at a 35rem measure; 1.02rem on phones.

sheet-title.purpose: Docs page H1, max 22ch; clamp(1.9rem, 8.5vw, 2.4rem) at width 116% on phones.

sheet-heading.purpose: Docs H2, always under a 3px ink rule.

label-small.purpose: ON THIS PAGE, ledger group titles, PREVIOUS/NEXT, search result tags, alert titles, table headers.

tab-label.purpose: Vertical uppercase labels on the binder's index tabs.

side-title.purpose: Playground order-column headings (Basket, Your order, Profile) with a mono count beside them.

action.purpose: The Pay button's label and the total inside it, tabular numerals.

switch-label.purpose: The X-RAY word on the playground's primary switch; the one wide label large enough to read as a control.

annotation.purpose: X-ray tag names, DispatchResult lamps and tape readouts in mono 700; render counts at 600, 0.74rem.

motion.name: beat
motion.purpose: The single page clock: quack (2 beats), bubble wipe (1.5), answer rise (1.5, staggered by 1/3 and 2/3 beat), split-flap letters and lamps (0.7), dispatcher drain (1 per action), copied state (5).

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Expo-out curve for every beat-driven animation and transform.

motion.name: state-swap
motion.purpose: Background/color swap on chips and ledger rows on hover. Docs tabs and pager cards swap over one beat instead.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All animations and transitions collapse under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: tab-pull
motion.value: translateX(3px) hover / 6px press over one beat
motion.purpose: Docs index tabs slide out of the binder (upward 3px/5px when along the top edge).

motion.name: xray-reveal
motion.value: calc(var(--beat) * 0.6) with a calc(var(--beat) * 0.066) stagger per reading-order index
motion.purpose: X-ray outlines tighten from 16px to 7px offset and tags and render counts wipe in (pill-shaped clip) top bar first, tape last, all inside one beat.

motion.name: half-beat-swap
motion.purpose: Playground pill and Pay background/color swaps; the X-ray switch and its knob swap and slide over a full beat.

motion.name: drawer-dock
motion.value: translateX(2.5rem) to none with a fade over one beat (translateY at 1100px and below)
motion.purpose: The code drawer docking beside the shop, or rising as a bottom sheet.

motion.name: lampflip
motion.value: perspective(200px) rotateX(-90deg) to none over 0.7 beat
motion.purpose: The latest action's lamp in the tape and the current order step's lamp flipping in.

components.css: .ds-searchwrap { padding: 1rem; background: #FFD425; color: #17140F; font-family: 'Atkinson Hyperlegible Next', sans-serif; } .ds-search { position: relative; max-width: 26rem; } .ds-search input { width: 100%; height: 2.6rem; padding: 0 2.6rem 0 1rem; border: 3px solid #17140F; border-radius: 999px; background: #FFFFFF; color: #17140F; font: 400 1rem/1 'Atkinson Hyperlegible Next', sans-serif; appearance: none; } .ds-search input::placeholder { color: #4F4838; } .ds-search input:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #17140F; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-search kbd { position: absolute; right: 0.6rem; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); min-width: 1.5rem; padding: 0.12rem 0.4rem; border: 1.5px solid #17140F; border-radius: 6px; font: 600 0.78rem/1.2 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; text-align: center; } .ds-search input:focus ~ kbd { display: none; } .ds-results { margin-top: 0.5rem; max-width: 40rem; background: #FFFFFF; border: 3px solid #17140F; border-radius: 14px; padding: 0.35rem 0; } .ds-result { display: block; padding: 0.7rem 1rem; color: inherit; text-decoration: none; border-top: 1.5px solid #17140F; } .ds-result:first-child { border-top: 0; } .ds-rt { display: flex; gap: 0.6rem; align-items: baseline; font-weight: 700; } .ds-tag { font: 900 0.72rem/1 'Anybody', sans-serif; font-stretch: 150%; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #4F4838; } .ds-rx { display: block; margin-top: 0.25rem; font-size: 0.9rem; line-height: 1.45; color: #4F4838; } .ds-result mark { background: none; color: inherit; font-weight: 800; text-decoration: underline 3px #FFD425; text-underline-offset: 0.18em; } .ds-result[aria-selected="true"], .ds-result:hover { background: #17140F; color: #FFFFFF; } .ds-result[aria-selected="true"] .ds-tag, .ds-result:hover .ds-tag, .ds-result[aria-selected="true"] .ds-rx, .ds-result:hover .ds-rx { color: #CBC3AA; } .ds-result:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #17140F; outline-offset: -3px; }

narrative.northStar: The Rubber Duck on the Desk
narrative.overview:
The site is the conversation a developer has with the rubber duck beside their keyboard. The duck asks, on a field of drenched vinyl yellow; Ducky answers on a white answer sheet, in black ink and compiled code. Every surface is one of three grounds (yolk, ink, sheet), every stroke is ink, and a single beak orange marks the thing to press. Nothing is tinted, graded or lit: depth comes from swapping grounds and from heavy ruled lines, the way a moulded toy or a printed form gets its structure.

Density is generous at the section level (sections breathe at 4 to 7rem) and tight inside instruments: the dispatcher board is a ruled grid of fixed cells, the API list and package stack are ruled ledgers, and proof is a column of test names with check lamps. Display type is Anybody pushed wide and black, stamped like a toy's moulded mark; body is Atkinson Hyperlegible Next; JetBrains Mono appears wherever the reader is looking at something they would type or run.

Motion has one clock. A single beat (420ms, expo-out) drives the duck's squash-and-stretch quack, the speech bubble's wipe, the answer sheet's rise, the split-flap letters and lamps on the board, and the dispatcher's one-action-per-tick drain. Controls invert ink on press rather than glowing or lifting.

The documentation is the same world set as the duck's answer binder: yolk is the binder ground and its index tabs, the page being read is a white sheet in a 3px ink frame, ink is code, rules and the current tab. It runs denser than the home page (a reading ramp at a 35rem measure, small 3 to 8px radii on inline marks) but adds no new color, no shadow and no tint.

The playground is the same world as a working shop on the desk: the yolk ground is the desk, the shop is one white answer sheet in a 3px ink frame, and the inspector is the home page's ink dispatcher board docked to the bottom edge as a tape. An X-ray switch turns the shop into its own annotated blueprint: ink outlines around every region, yolk tag pills naming the Ducky feature, ink render-count chips, all arriving in reading order inside one beat. Code opens in an ink drawer docked beside the sheet, never over it. It adds product colours (only inside the duck silhouettes and their filter dots) and no new ground, shadow or tint.
keyCharacteristics: Three grounds (yolk, ink, sheet) and one action accent (beak); secondary text hues are darker or lighter shades of the ground they sit on, never decorative tints.
3px ink rules for structure, 1.5px hairlines inside tables and ledgers.
Wide, black Anybody display; Atkinson body; JetBrains Mono for code, API names, test names and the board.
Pills for every control, 14 to 16px corners for panels and code, a 22px speech bubble with a drawn tail.
One motion beat for the whole page; press = ink inversion.
Flat. No shadows, no gradients, no glows.
Docs: a yolk binder with index tabs on the white sheet's edge; ruled ledgers for every list of pages or headings.
Playground: a yolk desk with one white shop sheet, an ink inspector tape docked at the bottom, an ink code drawer docked at the side, and an X-ray layer of ink outlines and yolk tags.

rules.name: The Three Grounds Rule
rules.body: A section's ground is yolk, ink or sheet, full-bleed, and nothing else. Sections alternate grounds and separate with a 3px ink rule; no panel, card or band introduces a fourth ground.

rules.name: The Derived Text Rule
rules.body: A secondary text color belongs to its ground (on-yolk-2, on-sheet-2, on-ink-2) and exists for legibility. Never carry one ground's secondary hue onto another ground.

rules.name: The One Beak Rule
rules.body: Beak marks the thing to press, or an alarm (a dropped result, a warning or caution lamp). If two beak elements compete in one viewport, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Stamped Mark Rule
rules.body: Headings are Anybody at 820 to 900 weight and at least 112% width, with negative tracking. A narrow or light display setting is off-system. (The docs' H4 run-in in the body face is the only heading set outside the display face.)

rules.name: The Wide Label Rule
rules.body: Uppercase wide labels (Anybody 900, 150% width, 0.08em tracking) name an instrument's parts: column headers, table headers, ON THIS PAGE, ledger group titles, PREVIOUS / NEXT, search result tags, alert titles. They never sit above a section heading as a kicker.

rules.name: The Typed Things Rule
rules.body: If the reader could type it, run it or find it in a test report, it is set in JetBrains Mono; prose is never set in mono.

rules.name: The Printed Object Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, no gradient, no glow, no blur at rest. Separation is a rule, a border or a ground change.

rules.name: The Product Colour Rule
rules.body: A product hue lives inside the product's drawing (the duck's body, its swatch dot) and never becomes a fill, border, text color or ground in the interface. A duck is never drawn with a beak-orange beak.

rules.name: The Docked Panel Rule
rules.body: A panel that opens over the page (code drawer, inspector tape) docks to a viewport edge as an ink ground and never dims, blurs or blocks what it sits beside: no backdrop, no focus trap.

dos: Do build every surface from yolk, ink and sheet, and reserve beak for the primary action and the dropped state.
Do separate sections and rows with ink rules: 3px for structure, 1.5px inside tables and ledgers.
Do set headings in Anybody at 820 to 900 weight and 112 to 150% width with negative tracking.
Do set code, API names, package names, test names and live readouts in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals where numbers change.
Do make controls pills with a 3px border that invert ink on press and selection.
Do time motion in multiples of the single 420ms beat on the expo-out curve, and honour reduced motion.
Do pair every claim with its proof: code block plus named tests.
Do hold docs prose to the 35rem measure and let code slabs and tables take up to 60rem.
Do caption every docs code slab with its source file and its tested status.
Do keep the reader's place visible on every docs page: current tab in ink, current ledger row in ink, yolk lamp on the section in view.
Do dock the playground's panels to a viewport edge as ink grounds (tape at the bottom, drawer at the side, bottom sheet at 1100px) and keep the shop usable beside them.
Do annotate in X-ray with three marks only: a 3px ink outline at 7px offset, a yolk tag pill that opens the code, and an ink render-count chip; reveal them in reading order inside one beat.
Do show the app's own compiled source in the code drawer, captioned with its path, with the line that matters marked in yolk.
Do give every action in the inspector its DispatchResult lamp: yolk Reduced, beak Dropped and Failed, an on-ink-2 ring Vetoed.
Do draw products as the site's duck silhouette in the product's colour with an ink outline and an ink beak (yolk on a black duck).
Do state in the shop's first viewport that nothing is for sale and Pay charges nothing.
Do disable a control with a dashed on-sheet-2 border and on-sheet-2 text, not by fading it.
donts: Don't add shadows, gradients, glows or translucent overlays; depth is ground, rule and inversion.
Don't introduce tints of yolk or ink as fills; secondary hues exist only as text on their own ground.
Don't put beak on more than one element per viewport outside the dispatcher board.
Don't use cards with fills and corners as a layout device; use ruled ledgers and frames.
Don't set prose or headings in mono, or code in the display face.
Don't give a section heading a small label above it; headings stand alone.
Don't set inline code in docs prose as ink chips; use the yolk highlighter chip.
Don't style search hits with a fill or in mono; they are bold with a yolk underline so they never read as code.
Don't tint alerts by kind; the kind lives in the stamped title and its lamp.
Don't put a scrim, backdrop, blur or focus trap behind the code drawer or the inspector tape.
Don't let a product hue leave the duck's drawing and its swatch dot, and don't draw a duck with a beak-orange beak; beak orange belongs to Pay and alarms.
Don't show X-ray outlines, tags or render counts when X-ray is off, or use the tag pill as a decorative label.
Don't set the shelf as filled cards; it is a ruled specimen sheet of hairline cells.
